title: Basic statement: 是
explain: Use 是 (shì) to identify people or things. Do not normally use it to link a person to an adjective.
question: Which sentence means “I am a student”?
feedback: Use 是 to connect the subject and a noun.

title: Yes/no questions: 吗
explain: Add 吗 (ma) to the end of a statement to ask a yes/no question.
question: Which asks “Are you a teacher?”
feedback: The question particle 吗 belongs at the end.

title: Negation: 不
explain: Put 不 (bù) before a verb or adjective to say “not.”
question: Which means “I don’t drink tea”?
feedback: 不 comes before 喝.

title: Questions: 什么
explain: Use 什么 (shénme) in the position of the missing information.
question: What does 什么 mean in this sentence?
feedback: 什么 asks for information about a thing or name.

title: Possession: 的
explain: Use 的 (de) to show belonging; with very close relationships it can sometimes be omitted.
question: Which means “my book”?
feedback: The owner comes before 的.

title: Location: 在
explain: Use 在 (zài) to say where someone or something is located.
question: Which says “I am at school”?
feedback: 在 comes before the place.

title: Have / there is: 有
explain: Use 有 (yǒu) for possession or existence. Its negative form is 没有, not 不有.
question: How do you say “I do not have a book”?
feedback: Negating 有 uses 没有.

title: Numbers and measure words
explain: Use a measure word between a number and a noun. 个 is common, but not universal.
question: Which phrase means “three people”?
feedback: A measure word links the number with the noun.

title: Completed actions: 了
explain: After many verbs, 了 (le) can signal a completed event. It does not always equal English past tense.
question: Which sentence indicates a completed purchase?
feedback: The particle comes after 买.

title: Experience: 过
explain: Use 过 (guo) after a verb to describe having experienced something.
question: Which means “I have been to China” (experience)?
feedback: 过 expresses experience.

title: Comparison: 比
explain: Use 比 (bǐ) to compare two things or people.
question: Which means “Today is hotter than yesterday”?
feedback: The hotter day comes before 比.

title: Ongoing action: 在
explain: Put 在 before a verb to emphasize an ongoing activity.
question: Which means “I am reading a book”?
feedback: The marker appears before 看.

title: Ability: 会 and 能
pattern: 会 = learned skill; 能 = ability/possibility
explain: 会 (huì) commonly describes learned skills; 能 (néng) can describe capability or circumstances. Uses overlap in some contexts.
question: Which is a natural way to say “I can speak Chinese”?
feedback: 会 comes before the verb，说.

title: Because / so: 因为…所以…
explain: 因为 (yīnwèi) introduces a cause, while 所以 (suǒyǐ) introduces its result.
pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bú qù.
translation: Because it is raining, I am not going.
question: In 因为下雨，所以我不去, which part gives the reason?
feedback: The reason is introduced by 因为.

title: Asking about degree: 多
explain: 多 (duō) before an adjective such as 大 or 高 can ask about age or size.
question: What does 你多大？ commonly ask?
feedback: Here 大 refers to age in a common question.

title: Two actions: 一边…一边…
explain: Use 一边…一边… to say two actions happen simultaneously.
hanzi: 我一边听音乐，一边做饭。
pinyin: Wǒ yìbiān tīng yīnyuè, yìbiān zuò fàn.
translation: I listen to music while cooking.
question: Which sentence says two activities happen together?
choices: 我一边听音乐，一边做饭。
feedback: The repeated 一边 marks simultaneous actions.

title: Where: 哪儿
explain: Ask where someone or something is with 哪儿 (nǎr). Answer with 在 and a location.
question: Which asks where the book is?
feedback: 在哪儿 asks where something is.

title: Clock time: 几点
explain: 几 (jǐ) asks about a small number. 几点 asks for the hour.
question: Which asks for the time?
feedback: 几点 means what time (hour).

title: Wants: 想
explain: 想 (xiǎng) expresses wanting to do something. Follow it with a verb.
question: Which says “I want to drink water”?
feedback: 想 should appear before the verb 喝.

title: Descriptions: 很
explain: In a simple descriptive sentence, 很 commonly links a subject to an adjective. It need not always mean “very.”
question: Which is a natural simple description?
feedback: 很 can introduce the adjective 冷 in a simple statement.

title: Permission: 可以
explain: 可以 (kěyǐ) expresses permission or possibility in many beginner contexts.
question: Which asks permission to sit?
feedback: 可以 before the verb asks whether the action is allowed.

title: Already: 已经
explain: 已经 (yǐjīng) often signals that an action is already complete.
question: Which says “I have already eaten”?
feedback: 已经 appears before the action, while 了 marks its completion.

title: Each time: 每…都…
pattern: 每 + time unit + 都 + action
explain: Use 每 (měi) for each/every and 都 (dōu) to describe a regular action.
pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān dōu xuéxí Hànyǔ.
question: Which expresses daily routine?
feedback: 每天都学习 means study every day.

title: Together: 一起
explain: Use 一起 (yìqǐ) when people do something together.
translation: I am going together with a friend.
question: Which means “I go with a friend”?
feedback: 和朋友一起 means together with a friend.
